title: Final answer (1)
description: Essential Criteria: Correctly states the mechanical energy loss per bump after the 30th as mgd sinθ.

title: Final answer (2)
description: Essential Criteria: Correctly states the average loss per bump for the first 30 as [mg(L+29d)sinθ - μ mgs] / 30.

title: Final answer (3)
description: Essential Criteria: Correctly states the inequality condition for L as L > d + (μs / sinθ).

title: Energy conservation reasoning
description: Important Criteria: Applies the work-energy theorem correctly to relate the car's final kinetic energy on the incline to the horizontal sliding distance s.

title: Constant average speed condition
description: Important Criteria: Recognizes that constant average speed between bumps after the 30th implies equal kinetic energy loss per bump, derived from kinematics on the incline.

title: Total energy loss calculation
description: Important Criteria: Correctly calculates the total energy loss over the first 30 bumps as the difference between gravitational work and final kinetic energy before the horizontal section.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional Criteria: Verifies that all derived expressions have correct units of energy (or length for L).

title: Sign error in work-energy
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalizes incorrect sign in the work-energy equation for horizontal sliding (e.g., forgetting the negative work done by friction).

title: Misinterpreting constant speed
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalizes assuming constant velocity (instead of constant average speed) or misapplying the condition to derive the per-bump loss.
